desc: Parse input and for each cake compute its maximum value across the three attributes and the coordinate achieving that maximum.
Sort cakes by maximum value descending and take the first 2K as the initial selection; compute the total sum and the parity of the coordinate counts.
If the parity is already even, output the total sum.

Verify the computation of the four possible loss values (min1, min2, min3, min4) and confirm they correctly represent the minimum loss when fixing the parity by reassigning one selected cake or swapping one selected cake with one unselected cake.

Confirm that when the best loss remains INF (no valid operation), the program does not produce a negative result; instead it should output the unconstrained total (which may be suboptimal but indicates a bug if reached). Investigate whether such a case can actually occur and, if not, add an assertion or alternative handling.
Run the solution on the provided sample inputs to confirm it outputs 12, 209, and 333 respectively.
Wrap logic in solve() and test on provided samples to ensure correctness.
Verify on additional random test cases with small N via brute force to ensure correctness in all edge cases.
Optimize the set membership check for `S_indices` to O(1) using a boolean array instead of a set for better performance, though current complexity is acceptable for N ≤ 10^5.
